title: Henselian completion rigidity on the open complement
statement:
Let $C$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $I\subseteq C$ be an ideal such that $(C,I)$ is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Put $\widehat C=\varprojlim_{r\geq1}C/I^r$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $\widehat X=\operatorname{Spec}\widehat C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $U=X\setminus V(I)$, and $\widehat U=\widehat X\times_XU$, where $V(I)$ is the set of primes containing $I$. Let $\pi_U:\widehat U\to U$ be the restriction of the canonical completion morphism. For every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on the small etale site of $U$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] and every integer $q\geq0$, the canonical inverse-image map is an isomorphism
$$H^q(U_{\mathrm{et}},F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(\widehat U_{\mathrm{et}},\pi_U^{-1}F).$$
Here inverse image and etale cohomology are [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], and torsion means that each local section is locally killed by a positive integer. There is no excellence, regularity, or constructibility hypothesis. These are the canonical pullback maps, natural in $F$.

source.place: Expose XX section 4.4, printed pp.373--374: abelian comparison to completion (CTC); its Noetherian case is the Fujiwara--Gabber formal base-change theorem, Fujiwara 1995 Corollary 6.6.4. The present cohomology formulation is its open-complement form; in the strictly local case used by the item it is exactly the displayed assertion (*) on p.373.

proof.text: Every ideal of the Noetherian ring $C$ is finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], so $I$ is finitely generated. Set $A=C$, $A^{\prime}=\widehat C$ and $F^{\prime}=\pi_U^{-1}F$. The henselian-pair hypothesis and the torsion hypothesis are exactly those of [lem-per-admissible-modification-cohomology-presentation]. It supplies the common closed-fibre limit topos $\mathcal T$, the exchange maps $\alpha_q:L_F^q\to L_{F^{\prime}}^q$, and a morphism of first-quadrant spectral sequences $H^p(\mathcal T,L_F^q)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(U,F)$ and $H^p(\mathcal T,L_{F^{\prime}}^q)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(\widehat U,F^{\prime})$. Its abutment map is the specified canonical pullback, with compatible finite filtrations.

source.place: Expose XX section 4.4, printed pp.373--374, CTC and the admissible-blowup limit spectral sequence (**), followed by the henselian valued-field reduction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-admissible-modification-valuative-stalks] to this pair and sheaf. At each point $t$ of its conservative subfamily, the stalk of $\alpha_q$ is the cohomology pullback for $K_t\hookrightarrow K_t^{\prime}$ with coefficients $G_t$. Both valuation rings are henselian, the valuations are nontrivial, the inclusion induces the subfield topology and is dense, and $G_t$ is torsion. Thus [lem-per-dense-henselian-field-etale-comparison] applies in every degree $q$ and makes this stalk map an isomorphism. Conservativity of that subfamily now makes every $\alpha_q$ an isomorphism of sheaves.

source.place: Expose XX section 4.4, printed pp.373--374, CTC and the admissible-blowup limit spectral sequence (**), followed by the henselian valued-field reduction.

proof.text: Applying the cohomology functor $H^p(\mathcal T,-)$ to $\alpha_q$ and its inverse gives inverse maps, so the spectral-sequence morphism of Step 1 is an isomorphism on $E_2$ in every bidegree. By [lem-sp-page-induction] it is an isomorphism on all later pages, hence on the stable terms $E_\infty^{p,q}$. First-quadrant vanishing ensures stabilization: for $r>\max(p,q+1)$ both the incoming and outgoing differentials at $(p,q)$ have an endpoint outside the quadrant.

source.place: Tag 011M (section-spectral-sequence), page recursion; Tag 011N (definition-spectral-sequence); ILO XX 4.4, printed p.373, morphism of (**)lim.

proof.text: For each $n\geq0$, the presentation in Step 1 identifies these stable maps with the maps on the $n+1$ graded pieces of the finite filtrations of the two $H^n$ groups. Apply [lem-sp-finite-filtration-induction] to the canonical filtered pullback: its graded maps are isomorphisms by Step 3, so it is an isomorphism. The presentation and the stalk comparisons are natural in $F$; throughout we used their specified exchange maps, so this proves naturality for the canonical pullback maps in the statement.

The proof follows this sketch. The presentation states it over the closed fibre for a general henselian pair, which is plausible by proper base change for henselian pairs plus the Leray sequence for j_J. No SGA is cited. Step 1: Noetherian gives I finitely generated, and the presentation's hypotheses match (U' equals the item's hat-U, F' is the inverse image); its abutment map is the canonical pullback including the filtrations. Step 2: the valuative-stalks conclusions are exactly the hypotheses of the dense-field comparison, which gives cohomology isomorphisms for every torsion G and every q; conservativity then makes alpha_q an isomorphism. Step 3: the E2 map is H^p(T, alpha_q), so it is an isomorphism; page induction gives all later pages and E_infinity. First-quadrant stabilisation for r > max(p, q+1) checked. Step 4: the filtration of H^n has n+1 pieces, bounds (0, n+1), and the finite-filtration criterion applies in Ab. Edge cases checked: nilpotent I or zero ring (U empty), n = 0, C already complete, torsion not invertible on X. The duplicate search found nothing.
